label: script
not_in_script: examination: the script is an actor's brief that ends when the doctor examines; it lists what to examine and gives NO finding, so the card holds none
safety_net: the script gives none beyond a review at three months
must_not_miss marks thyroid disease and iron deficiency: the script says both must stay on the list; neither is an emergency
no swelling in the neck and no trouble swallowing: from the script's marking scheme, not from its background paragraph
the opening words are the first sentences of the script's read-aloud part

scenario.reasoning: A woman of 48 with a year of broken sleep, night sweats, erratic heavy periods, low mood, lost words, aching joints and exhaustion, told as separate complaints: the perimenopause, with thyroid disease and iron deficiency kept on the list. She thinks it is her thyroid and fears something worse. A learner is most likely to miss the past migraine with aura, which changes the safe route for hormone replacement.

patient.name: Ms Sarah Whitfield
patient.manner: Capable and articulate, apologises for taking up time, and understates what embarrasses her unless she is asked directly and without fuss.

scenario.opening_words: I'm not really sure where to start, so I'll just go from the beginning. For about a year now I haven't been sleeping.

facts.fact: I go off to sleep fine, and then I am awake at three, wide awake, and soaked through. I have to change my top. Then I lie there until the alarm goes.
My periods have gone completely haywire. Sometimes three weeks apart, sometimes seven, and far heavier than they ever used to be.
I am just not myself. I snapped at my daughter last week over absolutely nothing and she cried.
I have started losing words. In a meeting I could not remember the name of a colleague I have worked with for nine years. I write everything down now.
My hands ache in the mornings, and my knees as well.
I am exhausted all the time, even on the days I have slept.
Things with my husband, that side of things, has rather stopped, and I do not really know how to talk about it.
I saw somebody about eighteen months ago and they offered me antidepressants. I did not take them, because I do not think I am depressed.
My mum had a thyroid thing.
It has all come on gradually, over twelve to eighteen months.
I have drenching night sweats four or five nights a week, and six to eight hot flushes in the day. They are worst while I am working.
My last period was five weeks ago, and the one before came after a three-week gap. On the second day I flood, I use two forms of protection, and I once had to leave work because of it.
I have had no bleeding between periods and none after sex. My smear eighteen months ago was normal.
My mood is irritable and tearful, with a flat sense of dread in the mornings. I still enjoy things when I get to them. I have no thoughts of harming myself.
Losing words and forgetting names is worse when I am tired.
My fingers and knees are stiff for twenty to thirty minutes each morning. There is no swelling or redness.
I have vaginal dryness and sex is uncomfortable. I have urinary urgency, and I have had two urine infections in the past year.
In my twenties I had migraines with visual aura. They stopped in my thirties.
I have no other medical history. I take nothing regularly apart from occasional ibuprofen. I have no allergies.
I need no contraception. My husband had a vasectomy eight years ago.
My mother had an underactive thyroid and went through the menopause at fifty. Her mother broke a hip at seventy. There is no breast cancer in the family.
I have two children, fourteen and eleven. I drink a glass of wine on four evenings a week, rather more lately. I have never smoked. I stopped running about a year ago.
I have put on around five kilograms in the past year, mostly around my middle.
I have no swelling in my neck and no trouble swallowing.

scenario.ideas: I think it may be my thyroid, because of my mother. I do not think I am depressed. I think something is actually wrong.
scenario.concerns: I feel like I am going a bit mad. The losing of words is what frightens me most.
scenario.expectations: I want to know whether this is the menopause and whether anything can be done. I have read contradictory things about HRT and breast cancer and I do not know what to believe.
scenario.hidden_agenda: I have been reading about early dementia. That is what I am frightened of.

differential.diagnosis: Iron deficiency anaemia from heavy periods

investigations.reason: Heavy bleeding makes iron deficiency likely.
The family history, and symptoms that overlap.
A reasonable check at her age.

plan.step: Name the perimenopause and explain it in plain words
Discuss hormone replacement: because of the past migraine with aura, by the skin (transdermal) route, with a progestogen because she has a uterus
Vaginal oestrogen for the dryness and the urinary symptoms
Address the heavy bleeding in its own right
Cover sleep, alcohol, exercise and bone health
Answer the fear of dementia directly

data_gathering: Ask about hot flushes and night sweats.
Ask about the pattern of the periods, and about bleeding between periods or after sex.
Ask about mood, and about thoughts of self-harm.
Ask about vaginal dryness, discomfort with sex and urinary symptoms.
Ask about the family: thyroid disease, fractures and breast cancer.
management: Name the perimenopause and explain it.
Check a blood count with ferritin, and thyroid function.
Do not order an FSH: it is not needed over 45 with typical symptoms.
Discuss hormone replacement by the skin route because of the migraine with aura, with a progestogen.
Offer vaginal oestrogen for the dryness and the urinary symptoms.
relating: Find out that she fears early dementia, and answer it.
Make it easy for her to talk about sex.
Take seriously that she does not think she is depressed.
